messages:
alex: kicking off canary for release v3.14.0 -> model-serving. Rolling to 10% across eu-west1.
deploy-bot: Canary started: model-serving@v3.14.0 on pool 'canary-eu'. Instances: 6. Health checks: passed. Link: https://ci.redwood/run/5621
maya: noted. change window to 23:00 UTC, right?
alex: yep 23:00 UTC. pin policy: hold for 30m post-canary then decide. runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/backout-model-serving
sam: adding rollback criteria here: sustained 5xx > 1% over 5m OR latency p95 > 1.2s. If triggered -> abort canary + pin previous stable (v3.13.9) and start immediate rollback.
jorge: seeing small spike in 500s on canary host canary-eu-3 at 2254321180, not yet 1% but flagged. logs:
```
ERROR: grpc: upstream failed with code 13
path: /v1/generate
req_id: b3f7
```
maya: thx jorge. can we get a quick tail from proxy? `/kubectl logs -f proxy-canary-eu-3` to confirm
alex: running health check sweep and tracing now. hold any planned promos.
alex: decision: enter hold state for 10m while we validate. notify SRE if rate stays elevated. @opsbot please pin a hold marker.
opsbot: Hold marker placed by alex. Action: monitoring enabled, alert threshold lowered to 0.5% 5xx. Channel: #eng-oncall.
sam: if we hit 0.5% for 3 consecutive checks (1m cadence) we should abort.
deploy-bot: Canary metrics: 5xx=0.8% (5m), p95=0.98s. Autoscaler: stable. Rollout paused by human.
jorge: digging into a bad client shard. looks like malformed headers from a subset of requests. creating filter to drop malformed -> testing in canary-eu-3
maya: good. if fix works, we'll continue canary. if not, rollback. update release notes later: note the transient client issue and backout plan used.
alex: update: after filter applied, 5xx down to 0.12% in last 2m. resuming canary to 25%.
sam: ack. keep the rollback command ready: `curl -X POST https://deploy.redwood/api/v1/rollback -d '{"service":"model-serving","target":"v3.13.9"}'`
alex: opsbot to execute rollback if we cross threshold again automatically? opsbot: configured for manual only — will notify and provide quick-exec link.
opsbot: Quick-exec rollback link (requires 2-man auth): https://deploy.redwood/quickexec/rollback?svc=model-serving&to=v3.13.9
alex: good call. documenting final steps in runbook now. after deploy completes, we'll file a short postmortem and update changelog with backout rationale.
maya: thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
